newsitem.title: UK: Campbell & Armstrong to restructure firm.
newsitem.headline: Campbell & Armstrong to restructure firm.

text.p: Shopfitting group Campbell & Armstrong Plc said on Friday it was proposing to restructure, with a placing and open offer plus reorganisation of the firm's debt and a capital reduction.
Campbell said the proposals are aimed at reducing gearing and strengthening the balance sheet.
The planned reorganisation would see Campbell placing 65 million new ordinary shares at 5p per share to raise around 2.77 million stg. The placing is fully underwritten by Henry Ansbacher.
It also plans to make an open offer to qualifying shareholders of 14.44 million ordinary shares at 5p per share, on the basis of one new ordinary share for one existing ordinary share.

The open offer shares have been provisionally allocated to NatWest to satisfy a liability of 0.7 million stg owed to the bank by Campbell. The firm also plans to issue 10.6 million new shares to NatWest to repay 3.03 million stg owed to the bank.
In addition, Campbell also plans to issue 247,200 preference shares to NatWest at 100p per share to repay a further liability of around 225,000 stg owed to NatWest.
Campbell is also seeking approval for the appointment of Gil Thompson as non-executive deputy Chairman and John Cowburn as finance director.

The company also announced it had made a pre-tax loss of 7.98 million stg in the 13 months to January 31, 1996 compared with a profit of 0.2 million previously and said it would not be making a dividend payment.

Campbell said it expected that the temporary suspension of its shares, made on August 1 because of a delay in posting its reports and accounts, would be lifted following the publication of the prospectus and report and accounts. These have been sent to shareholders today.
